title: The Booking Machine

pain.statement: Booking one client means stitching together separate tools for the inquiry, the date, the contract, the invoice, the payment and the gallery, and chasing each step by hand.

evidence.summary: Guide describes the common setup of booking sessions in one scheduling app and delivering galleries in a separate gallery tool, and notes a popular scheduler has no built-in contracts and only basic payments.

A photographer-business blog says a popular client-management tool relies on a separate gallery integration, framing the setup as multiple tools and subscriptions. Competitor-adjacent source, weigh accordingly.
A gallery vendor's own blog explains how to pair it with a separate CRM, confirming that the two halves of the workflow live in different products.
News piece (Sep 2023): a photographer's video about chasing clients for unpaid invoices went viral and many photographers said they had the same problem.

caption:
Booking one wedding client shouldn't take six apps.

An inbox for the inquiry. A scheduler for the date. A contract you print, sign and scan. An invoice tool. A payment you chase. A gallery link you send twice.
None of that is photography.

Snap puts booking, contracts, invoices, payments and galleries in one place. Clients book from your page, sign in their browser and pay through your own Stripe. Snap takes 0% commission.
It is not magic: the Free plan has one session type, two contract templates and five active galleries. Lite raises session types and galleries; Studio makes all three unlimited.

Start free at snaphq.app
